topic: Which is the coldest desert on Earth? (Antarctica)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

wiki_antarctica.title: Antarctica
wiki_antarctica.notes: area 14,200,000 km²; coldest, driest, windiest continent; mainly a polar desert; interior receives less than 50 mm per year; about 70% of the world's freshwater reserves are frozen in Antarctica; lowest natural air temperature on Earth −89.2 °C at Vostok Station, 21 July 1983

discovering_antarctica.publisher: Discovering Antarctica (British Antarctic Survey / Royal Geographical Society / FCDO)
discovering_antarctica.title: Antarctica's climate: the key factors
discovering_antarctica.notes: the continent is a polar desert; precipitation mostly snow, averaging less than 50 mm a year (water equivalent) across much of the interior — 'hyper arid', like the Sahara; cites the Vostok record of 21 July 1983

wmo_archive.title: World Weather and Climate Extremes Archive — lowest temperature

nsidc_ice_sheets.publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC, University of Colorado / NASA)
nsidc_ice_sheets.title: Ice sheet quick facts
nsidc_ice_sheets.notes: Antarctic Ice Sheet covers almost 14 million km²; together with Greenland holds more than 99 % of land ice and over 68 % of the fresh water on Earth

aurora_desert.title: Is Antarctica a desert? YES.
aurora_desert.notes: largest desert (14 million km²), interior under 50 mm/yr; Sahara 9.2 million km² — corroboration only

claims.text: Antarctica is a polar desert — the coldest and driest continent; a desert is defined by low precipitation, and the Antarctic interior receives less than 50 mm (water equivalent) a year.
vo: which is the coldest desert on earth
desert means dry: the interior gets under fifty millimetres a year

claims.text: Antarctica covers about 14.2 million km², making it the largest desert on Earth (the Sahara is about 9.2 million km²).
vo: fourteen point two million square kilometres: the largest desert of all

claims.text: The Antarctic ice sheet is the largest store of fresh water on Earth (about 70 % of the world's fresh water; NSIDC: Antarctica and Greenland together hold over 68 %).
vo: its ice is the planet's biggest store of fresh water

claims.text: The lowest natural air temperature ever measured on Earth is −89.2 °C, at Vostok Station, Antarctica, on 21 July 1983 (WMO-recognised record).
vo: earth's coldest air was measured here: minus eighty-nine point two degrees, at vostok
screen: Coldest air ever measured on Earth.

myths.reality: Deserts are defined by low precipitation; Antarctica's interior is drier than much of the Sahara.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

landscape.our_gap: The feed answers 'Antarctica' over penguin footage; nobody turns a globe to the pole and puts the 50 mm / 14.2 M km² / −89.2 °C numbers on the continent itself.
